NONE: › a member of an unofficial military group that is trying to change the government by making sudden, unexpected attacks on the official army forces
遊擊隊員
› using unusual methods to get attention for your ideas, products, etc.
出奇制勝的，用奇招的

example: A small band of guerrillas has blown up a train in the mountains.
一小隊遊擊隊員炸毀了山區的一列火車。

NONE: › the activity of growing plants without permission on land that belongs to someone else or on public land, with the aim of improving the environment or producing vegetables or flowers for people to use or enjoy
（未經允許在其他人或公共擁有的土地上進行種植，目的是為了改善環境或生產蔬菜花卉供人使用或欣賞的）遊擊隊式園藝
A2 to give an answer to a particular question when you do not have all the facts and so cannot be certain if you are correct
猜測，推測，估計
B1 an attempt to give the right answer when you are not certain if you are correct
猜測，推測
A2 to give the correct answer or make the correct judgment
猜中，猜對，猜到
› used before telling someone something interesting or surprising
（用來告訴某人有趣或令人驚奇的事情）你猜怎麼著?
› used when you believe something is true or likely but are not certain
（表示沒有把握）我想，我認為
› someone's opinion about something that is formed without any knowledge of the situation
猜想
› If a piece of information is anyone's guess, no one knows it.
誰也不知道，誰也拿不準

example: I didn't know the answer, so I had to guess.
我不知道答案，所以只好猜了。
On the last question, she guessed right/wrong.
最後一道題目她猜對／錯了。
[ + question word ] Guess when this was built.
猜一猜這是甚麼時候建造的。
[ + (that) ] I guessed (that) she was your sister.
我猜她是你妹妹。
She asked me to guess her age.
她讓我猜她的年齡。
[ + question word ] I bet you can't guess how old he is.
我打賭你猜不出他多大了。
She guessed the answer on her first try.
她第一次就猜中了答案。
"You have a new job, don't you?" "Yes, how did you guess?"
「你換新工作了，是嗎？」「對呀，你怎麼猜出來的？」
[ + (that) ] I guess (that) things are pretty hard for you now.
我想你現在的日子過得不太好吧。
Go on - have/make a guess.
來啊——猜一猜嘛。
Both teams made some wild guesses (= made without much thought), none of which were right.
兩個隊都是瞎猜一通，沒有一個猜對的。
"I wonder why she's not here." "My guess is that her car has broken down."
「我奇怪她為甚麼不在這兒。」「我猜她的車拋錨了吧。」
"So what's going to happen now?" "That's anyone's guess."
「那現在又會發生甚麼呢？」「那誰知道。」

NONE: › to try to imagine something when you have little knowledge or experience of it
猜測，推測，想像

example: There are no photographs of him, so we can only guess at what he looked like.
沒有他的照片，所以我們只能猜測他的長相。

NONE: › an approximate calculation of the size or amount of something when you do not know all the facts
大概估計，粗略估算

example: Current guesstimates are that the company's turnover will increase by six percent this year.
按照目前的大致估測，這家公司的營業額今年會增長6%。

NONE: › the process of making a guess when you do not know all the facts
猜測，推測，猜想

example: The projected sales figures are pure guesswork on our part.
這些預計的銷售數字僅僅是我們一方的推測。

NONE: A2 a person who is staying with you, or a person you have invited to a social occasion, such as a party or a meal
客人，賓客
› If a person, especially an entertainer, guests on a programme or show, they are invited to appear or perform on it.
（尤指娛樂演員）當特約演員，作為特約演員參加
A2 a person who is staying in a hotel
（飯店的）旅客，宿客
B2 a person, such as an entertainer, who has been invited to appear on a television or radio programme or in a performance
（廣播電視節目中的）特邀嘉賓，特別來賓；客串演員

example: 150 guests were invited to the wedding.
150位客人被邀參加婚禮。
We have guests staying this weekend.
有客人到家來和我們一起度週末。
Is he on the guest list?
他在不在賓客名單上？
UK He is a paying guest (= he pays for the use of a room in someone's home).
他是個寄宿房客。
We would like to remind all our guests to leave their keys at reception before they depart.
我們要提醒所有客人在離開前將房間鎖匙交還到服務臺。
Our special guest on the programme tonight is Robert de Niro.
今晚我們節目請到的特别嘉賓是勞勃‧狄尼洛。
Madonna made a guest appearance at the concert.
瑪丹娜擔任了那場音樂會的特別嘉賓。
Simon Rattle will be the guest conductor with the London Symphony Orchestra.
西蒙‧拉特爾將在倫敦交響樂團擔任客席指揮。
He guests on their latest video.
他在他們最近錄製的節目裡擔任特別嘉賓。

NONE: › a type of beer that is made by a different company from the one that normally supplies the beer in a bar, and is sold in the bar for a short time
貴賓啤酒（由不同於普通啤酒的供應商供應，通常只在一段短時間內在酒吧銷售的特製啤酒）
› a book in which people write their names and addresses when they have been staying at a hotel
（旅館的）客人登記簿
› the most important person at a social occasion
貴賓

example: The prime minister was the guest of honour at the dinner.
首相作為貴賓出席了晚宴。

NONE: › a bedroom in a house for visitors to sleep in
客房（私人住宅中留給客人用的房間）
› a person who lives and works in a foreign country for a limited period of time, doing low-paid and usually unskilled work
（短期在一個國家通常從事低報酬、技術含量不高的工作的）外籍勞工
› mainly UK a small, cheap hotel
小客棧，廉價客店
› mainly US a small house near a larger one, where guests who are invited to the larger house can stay
客房（大型私人住宅邊留給客人用的小屋子）
